main_text.p: ma nominabátur, definitionis generalis altera, altera fpecialis fubinde partitionis, Híc λογικώτε-ρον ἢ πλατωνικώτερον, tota perpetuaq; artis forma duob.finib.terminifq; finitur ac terminatur, ᾧτι ἢ ἀπείρια, fine & infinitate: In Phædro illud πρῶτον ἢ ὕστατον, primum & extremū dicebatur: Cŏprehensa aūt duob.his finib. intermedia genera proprio nomine hîc nō appellátur, q ἀντάλλαξ Aristoteli antea fuerunt. Ergo cùm hæc omnia homogeneorū genera constiterint,ideæ, 10 quę fuerát in Phædro appellantur paulò secús: Primo loco una exigitur,generalis nēpe & universalis definitio, quá Socrates ideo nos inven turos affirmat,quia ea fine dubio inest: Secundo loco διχοτομία generū postulatur, si sit: illa enim est difficultas,de qua in categoria distributionis tractatum est. Quapropter si perfectus ille distributionis numerus defuerit: quemvis alium proximum Socrates permittit: & hîc non secunda idea, sed duæ,tres, aut quotlibet á Socrate dicuntur: Tertió ut distributa genera rursus pariter & definiantur & distribuátur ad extremam ufq; infinitorum multitudinem, pręcipitur, donec propositum initio totum subjectū genus modis omnibus exploratum & perspectum fit: non solùm quæ unitas, & quæ multitudo, sed etiá quám multiplex in eo quidq; fit: infinitatis autem idea (qui terminus infimus est) non priús ad cōcludendum adhibeatur, quám totus intermediorum & subalternorū generū numerus tractatus & explicatus fit: Postremó infinitorū & individuorū multitudo rejiciēda.

page.notes: Line numbers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and a number 30 appear in the margin; the Greek is transcribed as best read from the scan. The word "hîc" at the foot is a catchword. Several Greek words are uncertain and may need checking.
